parts.markdown:
Use our free Virginia paycheck calculator to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Virginia income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Whether you work in Richmond, Virginia Beach, Arlington, Norfolk or another Virginia community, understanding your net earnings can help you compare employment opportunities, manage household expenses and establish realistic savings goals.

## How to Use the Virginia Paycheck Calculator

Choose annual salary or hourly wages and select the pay schedule shown on your pay stub. Hourly employees can enter their regular hours and qualifying overtime.

Enter the federal and Virginia income tax withheld for that pay period. Use the full withholding amounts, including any additional withholding.



Include employee retirement contributions, eligible health premiums and other deductions from the same pay period. Enter each deduction once.

Enter prior year-to-date taxable wages if you are approaching a Social Security or Additional Medicare threshold.


## Virginia Payroll Taxes in 2026

The [Virginia Department of Taxation](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/withholding-tax) publishes official income tax information and employer withholding instructions.

## Virginia Income Tax Brackets

Virginia uses progressive individual income tax rates.

Its employer withholding formula applies the following rates to annualized taxable income after applicable deductions and exemptions.

Your highest marginal income tax rate does not apply to every dollar of gross earnings.

Employers calculate withholding according to the official Virginia employer withholding instructions.

## Understanding Virginia Form VA-4

Virginia employees generally complete Form VA-4 to communicate their withholding information to employers.

The form records personal exemptions, eligible age or blindness exemptions and additional withholding requests.

Federal Form W-4 is separate from Virginia's withholding certificate.

Review your elections when starting employment, changing your household circumstances or determining that your existing withholding may be insufficient.

Current employer and employee withholding forms are available through the Virginia withholding tax resources.

## How to Calculate Virginia Income Tax Withholding

Consider an employee earning $65,000 annually and claiming one ordinary personal exemption.

Annualized taxable wages: $65,000.

Subtract the payroll deduction and applicable exemption:

$65,000 − $8,750 − $930 = $55,320.

The adjusted wages exceed the $17,000 threshold.

Annualized withholding:

$720 + (($55,320 − $17,000) × 5.75%).

Annualized withholding equals $2,923.40.

For 26 biweekly payments:

$2,923.40 ÷ 26 = approximately $112.44.

This example uses the exact employer withholding formula rather than approximate wage-bracket tables.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Virginia Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding depends on earnings, filing status, payment frequency and Form W-4 information.

Employers use the calculation procedures in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages toward Social Security, up to $184,500 in 2026.

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered wages.

Additional Medicare withholding of 0.9% generally applies when Medicare-covered wages paid by an employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Review [IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and the Social Security Administration contribution limits for official payroll requirements.

## Working Across Virginia State Borders

Virginia has reciprocal income tax arrangements with certain neighboring jurisdictions, including Maryland, Pennsylvania, West Virginia, Kentucky and the District of Columbia, subject to applicable conditions.

These arrangements are particularly relevant to employees commuting throughout the Washington metropolitan area.

Eligible employees may need to provide the appropriate documentation to prevent unnecessary withholding in their employment state.

Read the official Virginia reciprocity guidance before claiming an exemption.

Remote work and employment across multiple jurisdictions may require additional calculations.

## Does Virginia Have Local Employee Income Taxes?

Virginia municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes.

Employees working in Richmond or Virginia Beach therefore generally do not encounter additional municipal wage taxes.

However, housing costs, transportation, property taxes and other expenses can influence household purchasing power.

Compare estimated take-home pay and living expenses separately when evaluating employment opportunities.

## Managing Your Virginia Take-Home Income

Build your monthly budget using estimated net earnings rather than gross salary.

Include housing, transportation, groceries, utilities, healthcare and required debt payments.

Review the IRS retirement plan resources when considering retirement contributions.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) and [mortgage payment calculator](/calculators/mortgage-calculator/) can help establish realistic savings and housing budgets.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau also offers educational resources for managing household finances.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is Virginia's income tax rate in 2026?

Virginia uses progressive income tax rates ranging from 2% to 5.75%. Actual paycheck withholding depends on taxable wages, applicable deductions and withholding exemptions.

### How much is a Virginia personal withholding exemption worth?

Each ordinary personal or dependent withholding exemption has an annual value of $930 under the applicable employer formula.

### Does Virginia have local employee income taxes?

Virginia municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes. Federal and Virginia state payroll deductions still apply.
